tools.name: Antiseptic Swab
tools.description: Sponge stick loaded with skin antiseptic. The field is prepared from the planned incision outwards, never back over cleaned skin.

tools.name: Gauze Swab
tools.description: Absorbent swab for blotting the field so the tissue planes stay visible.

tools.name: Towel Clip
tools.description: Backhaus clip. Its sharp curved points pierce the drapes and lock, holding them in place around the field.

tools.name: Local Anaesthetic Syringe
tools.description: Syringe with a fine needle for infiltrating local anaesthetic around a wound before it is explored or closed.

tools.name: Scalpel, #10 Blade
tools.description: Number 3 handle with a #10 blade. The large curved belly cuts long skin incisions, with the handle held like a violin bow.

tools.name: Scalpel, #15 Blade
tools.description: Number 3 handle with a #15 blade. The small curved edge makes short, precise incisions, with the handle held like a pencil.

tools.name: Metzenbaum Scissors
tools.description: Long handles and short, fine, blunt-tipped blades, for dissecting and dividing delicate tissue.

tools.name: Mayo Scissors
tools.description: Heavier scissors for tough tissue such as fascia. Using them on delicate tissue crushes it.

tools.name: Suture Scissors
tools.description: Short straight scissors kept for trimming suture ends only, so the tissue scissors stay sharp.
tools.todo: Confirm straight Mayo scissors as the pattern drawn for suture scissors.

tools.name: Adson Forceps, Toothed
tools.description: Fine forceps with interlocking teeth at the tip. They hold a skin edge securely without the crush injury flat jaws cause.

tools.name: Adson Forceps, Non-toothed
tools.description: The toothed Adson's shape, with fine serrations in place of teeth. On skin they must be squeezed harder than toothed forceps to hold, and crush it more.
tools.todo: Add what non-toothed Adson forceps are chosen for, once confirmed.

tools.name: DeBakey Forceps
tools.description: Long atraumatic forceps with fine interlocking rows of teeth along the tips, for holding vessels and bowel without puncturing them.

tools.name: Babcock Forceps
tools.description: Broad, fenestrated atraumatic tips for holding bowel or appendix without tearing the wall.

tools.name: Kelly Haemostat
tools.description: Curved locking clamp for occluding a vessel or holding the end of a tie. Only the tip half of its jaws is serrated.

tools.name: Mosquito Haemostat
tools.description: Small haemostat with fine, fully serrated jaws, for small vessels and delicate tissue.

tools.name: Army-Navy Retractor
tools.description: Double-ended handheld retractor with a shallow blade, for superficial wounds.

tools.name: Richardson Retractor
tools.description: Right-angled blade for holding back the abdominal wall and giving depth of view.

tools.name: Weitlaner Retractor
tools.description: Self-retaining retractor. Its ratchet holds the pronged arms apart, so a small wound stays open without an assistant.

tools.name: Needle Holder
tools.description: Locking driver that grips a curved needle roughly two thirds along its arc from the tip.

tools.name: Skin Stapler
tools.description: Disposable stapler that closes a skin incision with metal staples, quicker than sutures along a long wound.

tools.name: Electrocautery Pencil
tools.description: Diathermy pencil for dividing tissue and sealing small bleeding vessels.

tools.name: Irrigation Syringe
tools.description: Syringe of warmed saline for washing debris and contamination out of a wound.

tools.name: Yankauer Suction
tools.description: Rigid suction with a bulbous, guarded tip, for clearing blood and fluid so the field stays visible.

tools.name: Veress Needle
tools.description: Spring-loaded needle used in the closed technique for establishing pneumoperitoneum before the first port.

tools.name: 10 mm Trocar
tools.description: Larger port, used for the camera and for instruments that need the extra diameter such as the clip applier.

tools.name: 5 mm Trocar
tools.description: Working port for graspers, hook and scissors.

tools.name: Laparoscope
tools.description: Angled telescope and camera. A 30 degree scope lets you look over and around structures a 0 degree scope cannot.

tools.name: Laparoscopic Grasper
tools.description: Long atraumatic grasper for holding and retracting structures through a port.

tools.name: Maryland Dissector
tools.description: Fine curved tips for teasing tissue apart along a plane rather than cutting through it.

tools.name: Hook Cautery
tools.description: L-shaped diathermy hook. Tissue is lifted away from anything vital before the current is applied.

tools.name: Laparoscopic Scissors
tools.description: Long-shafted scissors for dividing structures that have already been secured.

tools.name: Clip Applier
tools.description: Applies titanium clips to occlude a duct or vessel before it is divided.

tools.name: Specimen Retrieval Bag
tools.description: Impermeable bag so an inflamed or perforated specimen is removed without contaminating the port site.
